subject.title: fix(auth-health): prefer usable OAuth over expired inventory in provider status

question: Should provider-level auth status let a healthy OAuth profile mask missing OAuth profiles, or should this PR only ignore stale expired inventory while keeping missing auth visible?
rationale: Auth-provider status is an operator-visible compatibility surface, and the PR changes missing-profile precedence without maintainer-visible approval or real behavior proof.

options.title: Keep Missing Visible
options.body: Move missing precedence ahead of the healthy override, only mask expired stale inventory, and require coverage plus real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Accept Healthy Masks Missing
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept healthy OAuth masking missing inventory, but should record that status contract and add tests for it before merge.

options.title: Pause For Linked Scope
options.body: Hold this PR until maintainers decide whether the canonical badge issue needs this rollup fix, the cache-refresh PR, or both together.

recommendation.title: Keep Missing Visible
recommendation.body: Move missing precedence ahead of the healthy override, only mask expired stale inventory, and require coverage plus real behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent commits show direct work on auth-health/status alignment in the affected provider boundary.
